newsitem.title: GERMANY: Flood evacuation units race clock in east Germany.
newsitem.headline: Flood evacuation units race clock in east Germany.

text.p: German emergency rescue teams raced against time on Wednesday to evacuate areas along the Oder river after one dyke reinforcing its banks burst and others threatened to collapse.

Hundreds of border guards, 1,800 soldiers, local police and volunteers worked around the clock with 36 airforce helicopters to shore up the banks of the Oder, which forms part of Germany's border with Poland, German officials said.

Officials said they cleared about 250 residents in areas south of Frankfurt an der Oder and 300 at the confluence of the Oder and Neisse rivers, but that more of the area's 5,000 residents would have to leave if the river kept swelling.
They said water levels would rise by 20 cm (eight inches) during the day and that dykes were so porous large swathes of the area could be under water by early next week.
Across the river in Poland, officials said a new high-water swell was advancing down the upper Oder, some 300 km (180 miles) upstream, but was less serious than one earlier this month.

"The flooding is by no means over. There will be another wave. Those who are not able to join emergency teams must get out," Alwin Ziel, interior minister of the state of Brandenburg, said in a radio interview.
"Time is running out for the evacuation," Ziel warned residents who had ignored police orders on Tuesday to leave their homes.
Germany so far has escaped the worst of the flooding which has claimed more than 100 lives this month in the Czech Republic and Poland where thousands of homes have been flooded.
But German towns have been hit by power cuts and overflowing sewers and farmers have started moving thousands of livestock from the danger zone.
Government spokesman Peter Hausmann reiterated a pledge by Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who visited the area on Tuesday, to help in every way possible.
Hausmann said the cabinet had discussed the crisis in the morning and decided to earmark a 200 million mark ($110 million) reconstruction fund for the area once the catastrophe was over.
Defence Minister Volker Ruehe plans to visit the crisis areas on Thursday to oversee the rescue operation, a ministry spokesman said in Bonn.

The burst dyke flooded the area between the villages of Aurith and Brieskow-Finkenheerd just south of Frankfurt an der Oder, and police were evacuating the last remaining residents there, local authorities said.
Local officials said emergency reinforcements had been sent to help repair the nearly 100-metre-long breach. But after several hours they gave up to concentrate on maintaining dykes.
Further south, in villages around Ratzdorf near the confluence of the two rivers, rescue teams evacuated the last of some 800 residents with homes there, Ziel's ministry said.
He said police had also closed off large parts of the region to journalists in the interests of their own safety.
The Post Ministry said it was freeing up radio frequencies for flood announcements to rescue teams and residents.
German officials say it is too early to estimate the cost of damage in Germany caused by the floods that have incurred billions of dollars of damage in other parts of central Europe.
German insurance firm Allianz AG set up a telephone hotline for inquiries about flood damages and claims. ($ = 1.820 German Marks)
